sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Long-Haul Bonded Highway Freight Transport under TIR Carnets

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national, French-influenced Napoleonic tradition)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, freedom of establishment under Article 49 TFEU
Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment protection agreements jointly concluded with third states
Luxembourg national double-taxation treaty network, including DTAAs with Germany, France, China and the United States

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended, particularly Part I and the provisions on Sociétés à Responsabilité Limitée; Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as consolidated; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the register of beneficial owners (RBE); applicable EU AML Directives and Commission Implementing Regulations; and Luxembourg freezing-asset and sanctions laws transposing common EU restrictive measures.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / current official registry extract of each corporate shareholder and any corporate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or commercial register in the jurisdiction of incorporation, e.g. Luxembourg Business Registers for Luxembourg corporate shareholders or the equivalent foreign registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for states party to the Apostille Convention; otherwise consular legalization through the Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the articles of association of each corporate shareholder and corporate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registrar, notary, or chamber of notaries in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Apostille States, consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified passport copies of each beneficial owner, director, and manager of the Luxembourg SARL and of its foreign corporate shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent public authority in the country of residence or nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille through the competent Ministry of Foreign Affairs or competent authority of the source jurisdiction; consular legalization where Apostille is unavailable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French translation of each constitutive document and UBO support document not already drafted in French, German, or Luxembourgish
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translation certificate attached to the authenticated originals; no separate apostille required where originals are already apostilled

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The Luxembourg notary conducting incorporation and any AML/CFT obliged entity providing corporate or payment services must apply risk-based customer due diligence; must identify and verify all UBOs above 25%; must determine whether any UBO, director, manager, or counterparty is a politically exposed person (PEP), using internationally recognized databases and reliable public sources; must screen all relevant parties against the UN, EU, and Luxembourg national consolidated sanctions lists, the OFAC SDN list for USD clearing and US correspondence banking dependencies, and Luxembourg domestic restrictive measures enforced by the Ministry of Finance and financial intelligence unit; all screening results must be documented in the AML/KYC file and retained for statutory periods.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online portal; official RCS registry at www.lbr.lu, including the MyLBR e-filing service for name clearance and registration requests
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in French, German, Luxembourgish, or another language expressed in Latin-script characters and must be capable of accurate transcription in the RCS. Non-Latin names must be accompanied by an official transliteration into Latin characters. Names must include a legal form indication fully written as 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the recognized abbreviation 'SARL' or 'S. à r.l.'; the name must be clearly distinct from all existing registered names and must not be misleading as to the company's object or legal status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS clearance service rejects a proposed name, the applicant or its notary may file a written administrative reconsideration request through the Luxembourg Business Registers platform within 15 days of the rejection notice, specifying the grounds of compliance and submitting revised evidence of distinctiveness. If the administrative reconsideration is denied, the applicant may bring the matter before the competent chamber of the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement, commercial section) by way of summary proceedings or an application for judicial review of the clearance refusal. Extension of a valid name reservation is not generally available; after the 30-day reservation window expires, the name may be re-reserved on a fresh application, subject to intervening third-party priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: General Luxembourg corporate law permits a registered office to be domiciled through a licensed corporate domiciliation provider, provided the address is a real physical location in Luxembourg capable of receiving legal correspondence. However, for a licensed cross-border TIR road haulage undertaking under Regulation (EC) No 1072/2009 and Luxembourg transport licensing law, a mere virtual office is not commercially or legally sufficient; the undertaking must maintain an effective and stable establishment in Luxembourg with operational facilities, management presence, records of vehicle maintenance and transport documents, and personnel with genuine decision-making capacity regarding haulage activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. For a licensed Luxembourg TIR goods road transport operator, the estimated probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by Luxembourg transport authorities, labor inspectorate, or customs authorities is approximately 80 to 90 percent during the initial 12 to 24 months of active operation, because issuance of the operator license depends on continuing compliance with establishment, financial capacity, fitness, and professional competence conditions, and cross-border TIR operations trigger customs and road-worthiness spot inspections.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability verification and preliminary RCS name clearance application
Sworn French translation of constitutional documents of foreign corporate shareholders and UBO supporting documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for certified translation, charged per translated page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the SARL articles of association (statuts)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for notarial drafting of standard SARL constitutional documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial execution of the articles of association and confirmation of subscription and payment of minimum share capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff plus official disbursements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration application in the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS)
Mandatory publication of incorporation entry in the Electronic Collection of Companies and Associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Ministry of Justice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO registration in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
Apostille or consular legalization of corporate and UBO source documents for each non-Luxembourg shareholder
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the document's country of origin or Luxembourg Embassy/Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Applicable consular fee or apostille service fee, plus courier expenses

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC onboarding, UBO identification, PEP screening, and sanctions-list verification by incorporation counsel and notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for due diligence and compliance advisory work

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, consolidated version; Articles 179-190 governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); Article 1 on company types; Article 7 on the registered office (siège social), as amended by the Law of 10 August 2016 and subsequent reforms.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) signed before a Luxembourg notary, submitted by electronic filing through the LBR e-filing portal and published in the RESA electronic compendium
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed share capital is EUR 12,000.00; each cash share must be paid up to at least 25% of its nominal value at incorporation; the funds must be credited to a segregated escrow account (compte séquestre) held by the notary or to a company-in-formation bank account, blocked until RCS registration, with a bank certificate of deposit issued to the notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that each founder-subscriber subscribes to one hundred (100) shares of EUR 120.00 each, being the fully-subscribed share capital of EUR 12,000.00; each cash share is paid up to at least twenty-five percent (25%) of nominal value into the notary's segregated escrow account, and the bank certificate is accepted. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office (siège social) is fixed at 14 Boulevard Royal, L-2449 Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [First Manager] is approved and appointed first gérant with sole signature power; the draft Articles of Association are adopted verbatim; and the gérant is authorized to file all incorporation documents with the Luxembourg Business Registers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Legal Review of the Articles of Association and Corporate Governance Pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Luxembourg notary to prepare the French-language draft articles of association (statuts) for a SARL, including statutory clauses under the Law of 10 August 1915, registered office address, division of shares, management powers of the gérant, and any transfer restrictions. Founders review the governance pack, including quorum and majority rules, and provide KYC documentation.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association
Certified passport copies of each shareholder
Certified proof of residential address of each shareholder
Curriculum vitae and police record certificate (extrait du casier judiciaire) of the proposed gérant
Business plan and activity description for ISIC 5221 bonded cross-border trucking
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises formal Objections to clauses, revise the draft and re-submit for clearance; no registry appeal exists at this pre-filing stage, and the governing board must issue corrected instructions to counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution and the notary's segregated escrow account (compte séquestre)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary share capital account in the name of the company in formation or in the notary's escrow. Wire EUR 12,000.00 or at least 25% of each share's nominal value to the account and obtain a bank certificate (attestation de blocage) confirming the amount is credited, unpledged, and blocked for release upon registration.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of deposit and blocking
Escrow account wire instructions
Source of funds declaration for each subscribing shareholder
Bank statements supporting the source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a KYC query on source of funds or economic substance, provide sworn declarations with supporting bank statements; upon compliance clearance the bank reissues the certificate and the notary proceeds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders or their power-of-attorney holders appear before the notary. The notary verifies identity, legal capacity, and the capital certificate, then passes the notarized deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) together with the coordinated articles of association; the first gérant accepts office at the same sitting.
required_dossiers: Final coordinated Articles of Association
Capital deposit certificate from the bank
Passports and residence proof of all appearing parties
Notarized power of attorney if a founder is represented
Written acceptance of office by the first gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires rectification of inconsistencies, execute a supplementary notarial rectification act (acte rectificatif) before any RCS filing; statutory notarial fees remain regulated and are borne by the company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the authenticated copy of the notarial deed through the LBR e-filing portal under the urgent application procedure. Pay the electronic filing fee, obtain the RCS registration number, and receive the certificate of legal existence. The registry automatically transmits data to the tax administration and statistical office; legal personality commences upon registration.
required_dossiers: Authenticated copy of the notarial deed of incorporation
Statement of persons authorized to bind the company (RCS form A)
RCS registration application form
Proof of payment of the official state filing fee
Registered office consent form signed by the lessor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the application, file a corrective declaration or amending e-filing through the same portal; if the query concerns the deed itself, obtain a rectification act from the notary and re-file with payment of any additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, the notarial deed is automatically published in the RESA electronic compendium. The LBR then notifies the company by email of the publication reference; the company must retain the RESA extract as evidence of opposability to third parties and for subsequent administrative procedures.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
RESA publication notice and date stamp
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or erroneous, file a written request with LBR customer service for expedited posting; any rectified deed must be re-published to preserve third-party reliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, Customs and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des douanes et accises; Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the RCS-generated Luxembourg national tax number as the basis for registration. Apply to the AEDT for a VAT identification number (numéro de TVA), to the customs administration for an EORI number needed for TIR operations, and to the CCSS for compulsory social security coverage of the gérant and any employees.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Certified copy of the Articles of Association
Identity document of the gérant
Registered office lease deed or proof of establishment
Declaration of operational physical premises for substance purposes
Bank certificate confirming the paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax or customs administration queries substance or premises, submit the lease deed and photographs of the operational site; if VAT registration is delayed, obtain a provisional VAT number from the AEDT and continue TIR customs procedures under the provisional reference.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Mobility and Public Works (Ministère de la Mobilité et des Travaux publics), Transport Regulation Directorate
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence d'établissement d'entreprise de transport routier and Community Licence (Licence communautaire) for international haulage issued under EU Regulation (EC) No 1071/2009 and Regulation (EC) No 1072/2009

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 4 declaration/registration for truck depots, garaging and associated vehicle parking; a full Environmental Impact Assessment report is not required for pure TIR bonded trucking operations unless heavy-duty washing, chassis repair, coating, or fuel-storage modules exceed the thresholds of the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 June 1999.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 20 July 1999 on municipal wastewater discharges, with pre-treatment limits for COD, TSS, oils and hydrocarbons before any discharge into public sewers; VOC emissions: compliance with IED thresholds under Directive 2010/75/EU where solvent-consuming maintenance activities exceed 150 tonnes per year; fuel storage: double-skinned tanks with leak detection and secondary containment; hazardous waste (used oils, batteries, tyres) managed under ADR-compliant manifests and disposal certificates.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) issued by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) for the depot, parking area and office premises; structural load inspection certificate for parking decks, lifting equipment and repair bays; workplace clearance by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) confirming compliance with the Law of 17 June 1994 on occupational safety and health; municipal authorization for heavy goods vehicle parking and maneuvering if public land is used.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) - Luxembourg direct tax administration (https://impotsdirects.public.lu); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) - VAT, registration duties and excise administration (https://pfi.public.lu); Administration des Douanes et Accises - customs, TIR carnet control and export procedures (https://douanes.public.lu). Central e-administration portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://guichet.public.lu) for VAT returns, RCS filings, customs declarations and e-invoicing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute the SARL notarial deed of incorporation and file it with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through the Luxembourg Business Registers portal; obtain the RCS registration number, which is the primary legal entity identifier. Step 2: Obtain the Luxembourg corporate tax identification number (matricule) from the ACD; this number is allocated automatically upon RCS registration and upon the first corporate income tax declaration (Formulaire 600). Step 3: Register for VAT with the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu using the VAT registration notification (notification d'assujettissement) to obtain a Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU followed by eight digits. Step 4: Apply to the Administration des Douanes et Accises for an EORI number (format LU plus eight digits) and, where applicable, for TIR carnet holder authorization and an Authorised Economic Operator (AEO) certificate to obtain guarantees and bond waivers under the TIR transit regime. The entire procedure is performed electronically; non-EU-established applicants must appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative for VAT purposes, whereas EU-established applicants may register directly without a local representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The SARL is a Luxembourg-resident capital company taxed at entity level on its worldwide income under Article 159 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR); profits are subject to corporate income tax, the solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax, and distributions are taxable at the level of the shareholder. No US-style check-the-box or partnership pass-through classification is available for a SARL. Luxembourg applies a modified territoriality rule: income of a foreign permanent establishment and foreign real estate income is exempt with progression provided it is subject to a comparable tax. No tax-exempt zone status applies to a road transport SARL established in Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a check-the-box election. Relevant statutory elections for a SARL include: (i) election to form a tax consolidation group (intégration fiscale) under Article 164bis LIR to offset current-year profits and losses of Luxembourg-resident group companies; (ii) election to apply the participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains under Articles 147 and 166 LIR (Soparfi regime); (iii) election under Article 50bis LIR for the intellectual property box regime; (iv) election under Article 60 of the Loi TVA to form a single VAT taxable person (VAT grouping) with Luxembourg-established affiliates; and (v) under the ATAD-compliant anti-hybrid rules introduced by the Law of 21 June 2019, a taxpayer may make a compliance election in its Luxembourg tax return to align the tax treatment of hybrid financial instruments with the counterparty jurisdiction, thereby preventing the mandatory disallowance of interest or dividend deductions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Luxembourg Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) under the Law of 12 February 1979 (Loi TVA), implemented in conformity with Council Directive 2006/112/EC and administered by the AEDT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: A Luxembourg-established SARL engaged in an economic activity is required to register for VAT from its first taxable supply without any monetary threshold. The general small-enterprise exemption (Régime de la franchise, Article 170bis Loi TVA) of EUR 35,000 annual turnover is available only to small undertakings and is not available to the SARL because cross-border TIR trucking constitutes an economic activity with input VAT recovery and intra-EU and third-country transport elements. Non-resident carriers are subject to mandatory Luxembourg VAT registration without threshold when they make taxable supplies in Luxembourg, unless the reverse-charge mechanism, the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) or the TIR transit arrangements remove the local VAT liability.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC) e-invoicing, or digital stamping for B2B supplies as of the current law. Mandatory e-invoicing applies only for B2G supplies to Luxembourg public authorities, which must be submitted through the PEPPOL network and the MyGuichet.lu e-invoicing channel since 1 January 2022. VAT returns are filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu on a monthly, quarterly or annual basis depending on turnover, using the VAT 400 series forms. There is no real-time API clearance requirement; however, taxpayers must maintain a Standard Audit File for Tax (SAF-T) in an approved electronic format for submission upon request, and accounting records must comply with the Luxembourg Plan Comptable Normalisé (PCN) chart of accounts.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exemption with credit) is available under Article 148 Loi TVA for supplies of goods physically exported to a destination outside the European Union and for transport and ancillary services directly linked to those exports, provided the supplier retains documentary evidence of export. For a Luxembourg TIR trucking SARL, the cumulative criteria are: (i) the goods are transported under a valid TIR carnet and discharged at the customs office of the third country within the TIR operational period; (ii) an electronic export customs declaration is lodged with the Administration des Douanes et Accises under the Union Customs Code; (iii) the supply is made to a customer established outside Luxembourg; for B2B transport services the general place-of-supply rule under Article 44 of Directive 2006/112/EC applies, so services to a non-EU taxable person fall outside Luxembourg VAT and intra-EU B2B transport is reverse-charged in the customer's member state; and (iv) the foreign-currency freight proceeds are repatriated to Luxembourg and traceable to the specific export operation within the prescribed deadline.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Customs Export Declaration lodged with the Administration des Douanes et Accises under the Automated Export System (AES) of the Union Customs Code
TIR Carnet issued under the IRU guarantee chain, bearing the dated stamps and discharge certificates of the customs offices of departure, transit and destination
CMR international consignment note (lettre de voiture CMR) evidencing the haulage contract, cargo identification and delivery to the third-country consignee
Commercial invoice and freight invoice issued by the SARL for the transport service
Bill of Lading, truck manifest, or equivalent transport document where the trailer is subsequently carried by sea or air
Inward Remittance Certificate, bank SWIFT MT103, or fuel-card clearing statement demonstrating receipt of the export proceeds in foreign currency
Proof of TIR guarantee cover issued by the national guaranteeing association (Chambre de Commerce du Luxembourg) and the carrier's TIR carnet holder authorization or AEO certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating positions are subject to joint audit by the AEDT and the Administration des Douanes et Accises. Where the TIR carnet is not properly discharged, the CMR is incomplete, the goods are not shown physically to leave the EU, or the foreign-currency proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory period, the AEDT will retroactively claw back the 0% rate and reassess output VAT at 17%, together with statutory default interest and late-payment penalties. Administrative fines of up to EUR 125,000 may be imposed under Articles 62 and 63 Loi TVA. Deliberate fraudulent export schemes, including false declarations, counterfeit TIR carnets and fictitious exports, give rise to criminal prosecution under the Luxembourg General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung) and the Criminal Code, with imprisonment of up to five years and criminal fines of up to EUR 250,000. The assessment and clawback limitation period is five years, extended to ten years where fraudulent intent is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), national central bank of Luxembourg and member of the Eurosystem; the European Central Bank (ECB) as the supranational monetary and foreign-exchange reserve authority; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the competent supervisory authority for banks, electronic money institutions and payment institutions in respect of AML/KYC and prudential supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible. Luxembourg maintains no exchange-control restrictions between residents and non-residents. Free movement of capital and payments is guaranteed by Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and by the Luxembourg legal framework on payments and securities settlement. There is no distinction between capital and current account for currency convertibility purposes; TIR trucking revenue may be received and held in any currency without prior authorization from the BCL. Profit remittance is unrestricted from an FX perspective: dividends approved by the SARL general meeting may be transferred abroad via SEPA or SWIFT without exchange-control clearance. The only material restriction is tax-related: a 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax applies at source unless reduced by the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (0% for qualifying EU parent shareholdings) or by an applicable double tax treaty. Polish, German, French, Belgian, Dutch and other EU counterparty payments settle freely in EUR.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg does not impose any statutory surrender, repatriation timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Freight receipts from cross-border trucking under TIR carnets may be retained in EUR or in foreign currencies, converted at the company's discretion and held in Luxembourg or EEA bank accounts. No BCL reporting is required for the underlying freight transaction; the only possible reporting is statistical (BCL balance-of-payments data collection) and EU Intrastat customs statistics, none of which create surrender obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse de l'Épargne de l'État (BCEE - Spuerkeess)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Commercial Trade Finance Account
Operational Account / Cash Management and Trade Finance Account
Operational Account / FX and Treasury Line Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Under PSD2 and the Luxembourg Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services, EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) may passport into Luxembourg and provide multi-currency payment accounts, FX conversion, mass disbursements, fuel-card clearing and payment initiation for a Luxembourg SARL without a full banking licence. Legal constraints: (a) EMIs cannot accept deposits and must safeguard client funds in a segregated account at a credit institution; (b) the statutory capital escrow of a Luxembourg SARL must be held with a Luxembourg notary or with a Luxembourg credit institution, and an EMI cannot act as custodian of the constitution capital; (c) TIR carnet guarantee providers (the Automobile Club du Luxembourg acting under the IRU TIR guarantee chain) require guarantees or sureties issued by an authorized bank, not by an EMI; (d) an EMI account cannot support documentary letters of credit or bank guarantees required by commercial counterparties. Recommended operating model: hold the operational, payroll and fuel-card accounts at a Tier 1 Luxembourg bank for statutory capital, TIR guarantees and SWIFT MT103 clearing, while using an EEA-passported EMI (e.g., Airwallex, Revolut Business, or Payoneer) for selective fast FX conversion and small-value international disbursements, subject to the bank's treasury policy.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors are not statutorily required to appear physically in Luxembourg for account opening. The Luxembourg AML/CFT framework (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended, and CSSF implementing regulations) requires identification of the client, UBOs and authorised signatories using reliable, independent source documents, but it permits risk-based remote onboarding and video identification under conditions equivalent to face-to-face identification, supplemented by eIDAS-certified electronic signatures such as LuxTrust. In practice, a Luxembourg-resident authorised signatory or registered agent is highly recommended; some banks impose an in-person interview for non-EEA-resident managers or UBOs, particularly where source-of-wealth documentation is complex. For a Luxembourg SARL holding the necessary transport licence, with a registered office in Luxembourg, a video KYC call with the manager plus apostilled corporate documents, RCS-DBE extracts and LuxTrust/eIDAS-signed account forms is normally sufficient. A physical appointment at the bank's premises or at a Luxembourg notary may be required for the first execution of the account agreement if the client does not use an advanced electronic signature; this is a contractual, not statutory, requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or managing partner resident in a non-EEA jurisdiction or in a jurisdiction with elevated FATF or source-of-wealth opacity; substantial paid-in capital introduced through multiple interim accounts; potential PEP exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) Valid biometric passport and apostilled proof of residential address; (b) clean sanctions and PEP screening report; (c) Luxembourg RCS extract of the SARL and certified articles of association; (d) certificate from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, RBE); (e) source-of-funds evidence for the capital deposited in the notary escrow account, comprising account statements, sale agreements, inheritance deeds or liquidation distributions; (f) bank reference letters covering at least three years; (g) audited financial statements or equivalent corporate filings of the parent/UBO; (h) CRS/FATCA self-certification forms; (i) business CV, professional references and a notarially certified power of attorney to the Luxembourg-appointed treasury signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive or high-volume cross-border operations: trucking fleets, fuel-card top-ups, non-EEA driver advances and transit payments may be perceived as ML/TF vectors despite the standard industry risk rating.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) Detailed business plan and signed long-term logistics contracts; (b) complete fuel-card master agreements (DKV, UTA, Eurowag) with monthly consolidated statements; (c) TIR carnet issuance records from the guaranteeing association (ACL/IRU) and NCTS customs movement declarations; (d) Luxembourg fleet registration certificates, tachograph data and driver payroll records; (e) formal cash management policy, ideally zero-cash or a documented EUR 500 daily cap on driver advances; (f) declarations to the CNS (Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale) proving payroll substance; (g) an independent AML/CFT risk assessment prepared by a Luxembourg law firm or audit firm confirming the low-risk standard trade classification; (h) proof of Luxembourg VAT (TVA) registration and regular VAT returns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived absence of economic substance, e.g., a Luxembourg SARL with no Luxembourg employees, no operational assets and no physical premises, used as a pure invoice conduit for cross-border trucking.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) Commercial lease agreement for a Luxembourg office or operating yard; (b) transport operator licence issued under EU Regulation (EC) No 1071/2009 as implemented by Luxembourg road transport law; (c) payroll records and CNS social security registrations for at least the managing staff; (d) fleet insurance policies with a Luxembourg-authorised insurer; (e) minutes of board and general meetings held in Luxembourg with operational decisions; (f) official VAT, corporate tax and RBE registration certificates; (g) sample CMR waybills and contracts with clients in multiple EU jurisdictions; (h) bank statements evidencing continuous treasury activity through Luxembourg; (i) an organisational chart showing the Luxembourg-based compliance officer and transport manager.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the initial share capital of the SARL, the compliant route is to transfer funds to the Luxembourg notary's escrow account (dépôt de fonds) or to a blocked capital passbook at a Luxembourg credit institution. The remitting bank must execute a SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR transfers or a SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR, using ISO 20022 purpose code 'CAPC' (capital contribution) or 'EQUI' (equity) and a remittance reference containing the RCS number and the wording 'Share capital contribution - Société à Responsabilité Limitée'. The notary or receiving bank verifies that the payee matches the subscriber, that the source of funds is consistent with the incorporation file, and that no sanctions filters are triggered. No BCL authorisation is required. For subsequent capital increases, the same MT103/SEPA routing applies, with the notarial deed of increase referenced in field 70 or the remittance information. Supporting documents include the notarial incorporation deed, the RBE and RCS extracts, AML/KYC questionnaires, source-of-funds statements, and the notary's attestation of receipt, after which the capital is released for operating purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The Luxembourg clearing infrastructure offers the following outbound rails for the TIR trucking treasury: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR-denominated payments within the EEA, cleared via TARGET2 at the BCL and instant payments via TIPS/SCT Inst for urgent fuel and driver disbursements; (2) SWIFT MT103 for high-value or non-EUR payments requiring correspondent-bank clearing, with structured remittance information mapping each wire to the invoice, CMR reference or fuel-card settlement statement; (3) SWIFT MT101 for batch and mass disbursements, suitable for payroll and periodic supplier runs; (4) documentary trade instruments, including irrevocable commercial letters of credit issued under UCP 600 and standby LCs or bank guarantees, used to back TIR customs guarantees (ACL/IRU chain) and large freight contracts; (5) fuel-card clearing via DKV, UTA or Eurowag, whereby cards are accepted at European fuel stations and settled centrally through the Luxembourg treasury via direct debit or periodic wires from the operational account. For auditability, all outbound wires should be matched to the underlying commercial contract, CMR document and customs declaration; the storage of SWIFT MT103 confirmation plus the commercial invoice in the treasury file satisfies banking AML/CFT and Luxembourg tax evidence requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards in EUR/USD, EUR/CHF, EUR/GBP, PLN/EUR, HUF/EUR, CZK/EUR and other trade-related currencies, executed OTC with a Luxembourg credit institution under an ISDA or FX master agreement; fully permissible for a non-financial corporate treasury without BCL authorisation.
FX swaps (simultaneous spot/forward or matched opposite forwards) used for temporary liquidity bridging and rolling of maturing obligations.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic currencies where physical settlement is restricted, provided the counterparty is a licensed credit institution and the hedge has genuine commercial underlying exposure.

Plain-vanilla FX options and collar strategies (EUR call/put combinations) from the options desk of a Luxembourg bank, subject to a board-approved treasury policy and an ISDA/CSA documentation framework.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCS) permissible for hedging long-term EUR-denominated fleet financing with a foreign-currency component; must be documented under ISDA and treated as cash-flow hedges in the financial statements.

There are no mandatory hedging requirements and no BCL/ECB pre-approval for any of the above; the only limits are the company's corporate purpose, the board-approved treasury policy, and the prudential credit and onboarding requirements of the counterparty bank. All derivative instruments must be backed by an ISDA/CSA or a local FX master agreement and recorded in the annual accounts in accordance with IFRS or LUX GAAP derivative disclosure rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, P&L and annexes) filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after shareholders' approval; approval must occur within 6 months of the financial year-end. For calendar-year SARL: approval by 30 June, filing by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Coercive fines up to EUR 250 per day plus administrative penalties up to EUR 1,000; continued non-compliance can lead to court-ordered administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership data in the Register of Beneficial Owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), maintained by LBR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation within 1 month of the anniversary of the initial RBE registration; any change in shareholding or beneficial interest must be filed within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 125,000 and potential imprisonment for directors; separate administrative coercive penalties may be imposed for each late confirmation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax returns: corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year entities, filing due by 30 June of the following year; extensions may be granted by a tax adviser, typically until 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.2% per month (annual 7%); late-filing penalties up to 10% of the assessed tax; failure to file triggers tax assessment by official estimate ('taxation d'office').

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial standing declaration for the road haulier Community licence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Mobility and Public Works / National Road Transport Authority (Administration des transports)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the licence anniversary, and in any event no later than the deadline set out in the current licence conditions; proof of capacity of EUR 9,000 for the first vehicle and EUR 5,000 for each subsequent vehicle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension or revocation of the Community licence; administrative fines; termination of cross-border TIR operations until proof is restored.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (statutory auditor) is required when the SARL exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average workforce 50 employees. A parent SARL that controls a group also requires audit irrespective of size thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP per the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial companies and on the register of companies, implementing Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS may be voluntarily applied for consolidated/corporate accounts where permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year the SARL must confirm to the RBE that its beneficial-owner data remain accurate; this confirmation is due within one month of the anniversary of the initial registration. Any share transfer, direct or indirect, creating or altering a beneficial owner must be reported to the RBE within 30 days after the registration of the transfer in the Register of Members.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% maximum aggregate rate in Luxembourg City (17% corporate income tax, 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT, and 6.75% municipal business tax; rates vary by commune).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday for the trucking/logistics sector; applicable reliefs include the Luxembourg participation exemption (100% exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains), the 80% IP box exemption for qualifying intellectual property, the investment tax credit for new tangible/intangible business assets, and a robust loss-offset mechanism subject to continuity and anti-loss-trafficking rules over a 5-year lookback window.
